source_limitations: This inventory is built entirely from public DNS resolution (via public recursive resolvers 1.1.1.1 and Cloudflare DNS-over-HTTPS), public RDAP (.xyz, .autos) and public ATI WHOIS (.tn), public TLS certificate inspection, public HTTP/HTTPS HEAD-equivalent status checks, and certificate-transparency (crt.sh) queries performed on the observation date.

Public DNS queries do not reveal the complete private DNS zone. A provider or registrar control panel may contain additional records (internal-only hostnames, disabled/parked records, records with restrictive ACLs, or records not yet propagated) that are invisible to public resolvers.
Absence of a record from this inventory does not prove that record does not exist in the authoritative zone — it only means public resolvers did not return it at observation time.

Certificate-transparency (crt.sh) results are incomplete for six of the eight domains in this run — crt.sh returned HTTP 502 (rate-limited/unavailable) for darhijama.tn, fixpert.tn, idauto.tn, mythosprod.xyz, notrejour.tn, ssangyong.autos, and uthinachess.tn during this observation window after the first two successful queries (agribee.tn succeeded fully; fixpert.tn returned an unrelated 404 on a later retry). CT-sourced subdomain discovery should be re-run independently before INF-CF-2 for the domains that did not return usable data.

DKIM was not evaluated by selector enumeration (prohibited — brute-forcing subdomains/selectors is out of scope for this stage). Absence of a DKIM finding is recorded as UNKNOWN, never as 'DKIM disabled'.
Registrar and DNS-provider control panels must be compared manually against this inventory before INF-CF-2 begins. This document is a starting point for that comparison, not a substitute for it.

All WHOIS/RDAP registrant (owner) contact information has been redacted from this inventory per the data-handling requirement for this stage; only organisation-level/technical fields (registrar, nameservers, dates, DNSSEC state) are retained.

risks: HIGHEST PRIORITY FINDING: mythosprod.xyz itself has no working web presence. HTTP requests to the apex and www redirect to https://darhijama.tn/, and HTTPS fails with a certificate/SNI mismatch (SEC_E_WRONG_PRINCIPAL). This must be diagnosed and fixed at the origin web server (Coolify/vhost routing on the shared IP) before or during any Cloudflare migration — Cloudflare proxying would not fix a broken origin, and Full (strict) mode requires a valid, matching origin certificate.

DNSSEC is currently ENABLED and signed by OVH (DS record present at the parent .xyz zone). A nameserver migration to Cloudflare must coordinate DS-record replacement with the cutover window; switching nameservers to Cloudflare while the old OVH DS record remains published at the registrar would break DNSSEC validation for this domain. This sequencing must be planned explicitly in INF-CF-2 and executed per the DNSSEC steps already defined for INF-CF-5, not attempted casually.

coolify.mythosprod.xyz is already an active, presumably administrative, production DNS record. It must be classified NEEDS_CONFIRMATION and protected by Cloudflare Access (INF-CF-4) before or immediately upon proxying — it must never be exposed to the public Internet without Access in place.
No DMARC record.

Whether the six other proposed hostnames (app/api/watch/n8n/admin/files) are intended to be created before or during INF-CF-2/INF-CF-3, or later
